note: Advisory control crosswalk — a defensible STARTING POINT mapping commitwork's baseline checks to control frameworks (EU CRA Annex I Part II, SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria, NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5). It is NOT a substitute for your assessor's/QSA's control mapping; review before relying on it in an audit. SCOPE HONESTY: commitwork evidences only the TECHNICAL subset a code/dependency/runtime/SBOM scanner can prove — see each framework's `scope`/`catalog`. The organizational majority (governance, HR, physical, contingency, policy) is out of scope and must be evidenced elsewhere (GRC, e.g. Vanta/Drata). A check is 'evidenced' when it PROVABLY RAN on a product repo, by either signal: `category` (rollup repo.scanners.<category>.ran) OR the precise per-check status in the sweep's checks-status.json (pass|fail = ran; skip = requirements unmet, e.g. a runtime scanner with no live URL). Evidence sources beyond checks (ledger, annotations, the monitoring program itself, audit records, KEV/EPSS enrichment) also evidence controls. explicit uncertainty.

cra.name: EU CRA Annex I Part II
cra.scope: The 8 essential vulnerability-handling requirements — all within reach of a code/SBOM/monitoring tool.

items.1: Identify & document vulnerabilities and components (incl. SBOM)
items.3: Apply effective & regular tests and reviews

soc2.name: SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria (2017, rev. points of focus 2022)
soc2.scope: commitwork evidences the technical subset of System Operations (CC7) and Change Management (CC8), plus a few Logical Access (CC6) criteria. CC1–CC5, CC9 and most of CC6 are ORGANIZATIONAL (control environment, risk assessment, HR, physical) and out of scope — evidence them in your GRC platform. All 33 common criteria are listed so an export can name the ones no check or evidence source supplies; those are reported as not evidenced, never as met.

controls.CC1.1: Commitment to integrity and ethical values
controls.CC1.2: Board independence and oversight of internal control
controls.CC1.3: Structures, reporting lines, authorities and responsibilities
controls.CC2.1: Relevant, quality information to support internal control
controls.CC2.2: Internal communication of objectives and responsibilities
controls.CC3.1: Objectives specified clearly enough to identify risks
controls.CC3.4: Assessment of changes that could impact internal control
controls.CC4.1: Ongoing and separate evaluations of internal control
controls.CC4.2: Evaluation and communication of control deficiencies
controls.CC5.3: Control activities deployed through policies and procedures
controls.CC6.5: Asset disposal and data recovery protections
controls.CC6.6: Protection against threats from outside system boundaries
controls.CC6.8: Prevent or detect unauthorized or malicious software
controls.CC7.3: Evaluate security events to determine whether they are incidents
controls.CC9.2: Vendor and business partner risk management

nist80053.name: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5
nist80053.scope: commitwork maps the code/dependency/runtime/SBOM-evidenceable controls only. A FedRAMP Moderate baseline is ~323 controls and the full catalog ~1000; the rest (PE physical, PS personnel, CP contingency, AT training, PL/PM planning, MP media, MA maintenance) are organizational/operational and out of scope.

monitoring-program.when: the scheduled sweep produced a slice covering the product

audit-records.when: per-check run provenance (checks-status.json) exists — timestamped audit records of each control's operation

kev-epss.when: the slice carries KEV/EPSS enrichment (exploitation-ranked risk assessment)

toolAliases.note: Maps a rollup finding's `tool` field to the check id whose control mapping applies (finding → check → NIST control, for POA&M rows). Unlisted tools fall back to RA-5 (Vulnerability Monitoring and Scanning).
